classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that symmetry makes retained cylinder volume equal to base area times the central axial water depth, then connect that depth to the tilt using tangent.

content.prompt: A cylindrical glass of height 12 cm and diameter 8 cm is filled to the brim with water. The glass is carefully tilted so that its side makes an angle of $\theta$ to the horizontal. The glass is then carefully restored to an upright position.

spec.description: Superimposed upright and tilted open-glass side views share a lower contact point. The tilted sides are parallel, its water surface is horizontal through the lower rim, and its opposite side extends above that surface. Two restrained blue water fills preserve the instructional distinction.
spec.mathematics: The cylinder has height 12 cm and diameter 8 cm. Its axis makes angle theta with the horizontal. Diagram coordinates illustrate the geometry without supplying theta or any calculated height.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the theta label are visible; no numerical answer is shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Given $\theta=50^\circ$, what is the new height of water in the glass? Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

answer.short:
$8.64\text{ cm}$.

The upright height equals the mean retained depth measured parallel to the tilted glass's sides.
answer.worked:
Across the 8 cm diameter, the retained depth measured parallel to the glass's sides decreases by $8\cot\theta$. Symmetry of the circular cross-section gives a mean retained depth of $12-4\cot\theta$. The upright water height $h$ equals this mean depth because the volume is unchanged when the glass is restored.
$$\begin{align*}h&=12-\frac{4}{\tan\theta}\\h&=12-\frac{4}{\tan50^\circ}\\h&\approx8.64\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Given the new height of water in the glass is half the original height, find $\theta$. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
Half the original height is $6\text{ cm}$. Using the mean retained depth,
$$\begin{align*}6&=12-\frac{4}{\tan\theta}\\\frac{4}{\tan\theta}&=6\\\tan\theta&=\frac{2}{3}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\\\theta&\approx33.69^\circ.\end{align*}$$
